The fullstack frameworkfor Cloudflare and Next.js

Describe a resource once. Flare writes the table, the API, the validation and the admin screens, with auth, storage and billing already wired — then ships it to Cloudflare Workers or to Vercel, from the same description.

export default defineResource({

  fields: {
    name: field.string(),
    email: field.string({ format: "email" }),
    phone: field.string({ required: false }),
    status: field.enum(["lead", "customer"]),
  },
});

[ pick one ] Stacks

One description,
two places to run it

Your resources, hooks, policies, seeds and every component are the same on both. What changes is the database, the ORM and where it deploys — so pick for the database, because that is the part you cannot move in an afternoon.

Cloudflare Workers

default

Cheapest to run, everywhere at once.

Runtime
vinext on Workers
Database
D1 (SQLite)
ORM
Drizzle
Cache
Workers KV
Realtime
Durable Objects

A Worker runs in every Cloudflare location without you arranging it, and R2 charges nothing to serve what it stores. The trade is SQLite rather than Postgres, and a runtime that is not Node.

$pnpm create flare-framework my-app

Next.js on Vercel

--stack next

Real Postgres, real Node.

Runtime
Next.js 16
Database
Neon Postgres
ORM
Prisma 7
Cache
Upstash Redis
Realtime
not on this stack

Extensions, window functions and ranked full-text search; any npm package that assumes Node; preview deployments. It costs more, and realtime has no equivalent here.

$pnpm create flare-framework my-app -- --stack next

Compare them properly — including what each one cannot do.

[ 01 / 05 ] Create

Everything a real app needs,
wired on day one

flare create gives you a working app with sign-in, a database, an admin area and the Cloudflare bindings behind them, already connected. No choosing libraries, no glue code.

  • AuthenticationEmail and password, Google and GitHub sign-in through Better Auth.
  • DatabaseD1 with Drizzle, or Postgres with Prisma. Typed schema, migrations you can read.
  • DashboardTables, stats, import and export, and forms for every resource, from its descriptor.
  • Roles and policiesWho can read and write each resource, enforced by the API and the admin.
  • File storageUploads to R2 with type sniffing and size limits built in.
  • EmailVerification and password reset mail through Resend.
  • CachingA KV data cache shared by every colo, revalidated by tag on write.
  • RealtimeChannels and presence on Durable Objects, with a React hook.

[ 02 / 05 ] Look

Six themes,
so no two apps look alike

Pick one when you create the app, switch with flare theme mono, or set FLARE_THEME. Sign-in, dashboard, admin and home page all follow: colours, type, button shapes and even the sign-in layout.

Calm and centred, indigo accents. flare create my-app --theme default

Warm and rounded, sign-in as a card over the page. flare create my-app --theme coral

Plain and direct, boxed forms with pill buttons. flare create my-app --theme amber

Crisp blue, bold headings, social sign-in first. flare create my-app --theme sky

Black and white on a fine grid. flare create my-app --theme mono

Fresh green, sign-in beside a customer quote. flare create my-app --theme emerald

[ 03 / 05 ] Secure

Every way to sign in,
already built

flare create asks which to switch on. Each has its screens, emails and account settings, and a method you switch off is refused by the API, not just hidden.

  • Email and passwordWith reset links and email verification.
  • Magic linksA one-time sign-in link by email.
  • Email codesA 6-digit code, for people who'd rather not click links.
  • PasskeysFace ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello or a security key.
  • Two-factorAuthenticator apps with backup codes, or codes by email.
  • Google, GitHub, Apple, MicrosoftEach switches on once its credentials are set.
  • Read the auth guide

[ 05 / 05 ] Ship

Live
in one command

flare deploy migrates the database first, deploys the Worker, then sets any secret you're missing — nothing to configure on the dashboard. On the Next.js stack the same command runs the Vercel CLI.

Questions

Is it production-ready?

Flare is at 0.x: the generators, auth, admin and deploy are tested end to end on every release, but APIs can still change between minor versions. Pin your version and read the changelog before upgrading.

Do I need a Cloudflare account to start?

No. flare dev and flare start run everything locally, D1, R2, KV and Durable Objects included. You only need an account for flare deploy.

Can I edit the generated code?

Yes. Generated code lives inside marked blocks; everything outside them is yours and is never touched. Flare also tells you when you've edited inside a block, instead of overwriting it.

How is it different from Next.js on Vercel?

It runs vinext, Cloudflare's Next.js-compatible framework, on Workers. Flare adds what a Next.js app leaves to you: database, auth, admin, API, roles, billing and security, generated and wired together.

Can I change the theme later?

Any time: flare theme <name>, or FLARE_THEME in .env. Every screen follows, the admin included.
